prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: the single frame of the TENTACLE CLAW — the three-fingered pink tip of a grabbing tentacle whose arm is a chain of links.

The chip stays SMALL: a single compact subject of roughly 95×95 px — ALL its ink together covers only about 12% of the sheet area — floating dead-centre inside its cell so that most of every cell is EMPTY flat #51e018 key, with at least 60 px of unbroken flat key between the chip and every cell edge. The background must dominate: if the cell looks painted rather than a small chip on green key, the sheet is ruined. Design identity to keep exactly — a three-fingered claw tip about as wide as tall, fingers reaching UP and slightly open: a rose-pink flesh body (#e858a8) with a pale pink lit edge on the finger tips (#f8a8d8) and a deep magenta shadow under the palm (#a02870), the three fingers joined at a rounded palm base, all on a 1-px near-black plum outline (#3a0a2a). Supple, grasping, organic.

Rebuild it as a sprite sheet under this strict contract:
- On a CONTINUOUS flat pure bright green chroma-key background, exactly hex #51e018, identical solid colour in every background pixel: no gradient, no vignette, no shadow, no floor plane, no panel, no second green shade.
- EXACTLY 1 cell laid out as 1 ROW OF 1 (one single cell = the whole canvas) holding exactly ONE subject; the canvas IS one cell.
- Cells in reading order (left-right, then top-bottom):
  cell 1 = the subject seen whole. The subject lies within aspect 0.70:1 to 1.30:1.
- The sheet canvas measures EXACTLY 256×256 px. Produce EXACTLY 1 subject cells — no more, no fewer — and nothing else on the sheet.
- Each subject sits well inside its cell with at least 12 px of unbroken flat #51e018 around it and clean flat gutters between cells: no subject may touch or cross a cell edge; keep every subject within the inner 75% of its cell.
- CENTRING AND SIZE: the subject sits at the exact centre of the canvas and stays SMALL — a compact chip leaving a wide flat-key margin on every side; if the cell looks painted rather than a small chip on green key, the sheet is ruined.
- NO guide lines, NO cell borders, NO divider lines, NO frames, NO text, NO labels, NO numbers anywhere on the sheet — the cell names above are ordering instructions and must NEVER be drawn.
- Style: the finest retro pixel art for its native resolution — as much detail and inner structure as possible AT that low resolution, crisp hard-edged square pixels, chunky bold forms, a rich four-to-six step shading ramp lit from the top-left with careful inner detail and real material texture, clean saturated colours, a 1-px near-black outline on every silhouette edge, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no smooth gradients.

- ATTEMPT-2 REFINEMENT (attempt 1 died gate: cell 1 aspect 0.68 below the [0.70,1.30] window — the claw was drawn too tall and narrow): draw the claw WIDE and LOW — the three fingers fanned out sideways like an open hand, so the whole subject reads as wide as it is tall or WIDER, its width never below ~0.9× its height; shorten the fingers and spread them apart. Keep the same palm base, same colours, same small-chip law. Everything else in this ask is unchanged.

- ATTEMPT-3 REFINEMENT (attempt 2 died the SAME gate: cell 1 aspect 0.67 below [0.70,1.30] — still too tall): make the subject a WIDE horizontal hand, not a tall claw — the palm is a broad rounded mound and the three short STUBBY fingers splay almost sideways, tips reaching only slightly above the palm; the whole subject must read clearly WIDER than tall, about 1.1–1.4 times as wide as high, like a crab pincer seen from the side. Same colours, same small chip. Everything else unchanged.
negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, letters, labels, numbers, cell borders, guide lines, grid lines, watermark, signature, blurry, anti-aliasing, smooth gradient background, scenery, stars, cast shadow, drop shadow, multiple subjects per cell, empty cell, cropped subject, subject touching edge
